config.notes: NRSA benthic macroinvertebrate multimetric index (0 to 100); higher is better. EPA's Wadeable Streams Assessment MMI of six metrics scored per NARS-9 region, the same index in every survey cycle; EPA's own condition benchmarks are the published criterion it can be scored against.

config.caveat: Specific conductance carries natural carbonate geology as well as disturbance: a pristine stream in a calcareous valley can score low on this curve.
config.notes: Specific conductance; higher indicates ionic disturbance (worse).
Total nitrogen; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse). The total fraction, reported in every NRSA cycle, and the fraction published nitrogen criteria are written against.
Total phosphorus; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse).

NRSA fish multimetric index (0 to 100); higher is better. Eight metrics per NARS-9 region, several adjusted for watershed area, scored from an electrofishing sample; sites sampled by seining carry no index.

config.caveat: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.
config.notes: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.
Chlorophyll a; higher indicates algal enrichment/eutrophication (worse).
Turbidity; higher indicates more suspended sediment (worse).
Percent fast-water (riffle/run) habitat; more generally better for many biota. Ecoregion-dependent.
Percent sand and fines; higher indicates fine-sediment loading (worse).
Residual pool depth per 100 m; deeper residual pools generally better habitat.
Mean bankfull height; both incision (very high banks) and over-widening (very low) depart from reference. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.
Percent embeddedness; higher means interstitial spaces filled with fines (worse).
Wetland cover of the watershed (%) is scored on EASI's national screening method, Wetland extent, adopted because no other source supports this function here. Good >5%, Fair 1-5%, Poor <1%.
